description: One link, one tier: plx.around, plx.aggregate and plx.process read one link-tier rule (operating.ontology_tools._effective_tier), so a same-source FK link between staging rows keeps its tier in all three and a cross-source or text-join link to a gold_native_staging row is a lead in all three. Over a throwaway projection of one GET-only Portal reporting API sync into {tmp} (the L7 probe's build, no BC capture), scripts.link_tier_agree_probe takes up to 20 sales orders (those with a staging end first, then the lowest SHA-256 of a current SalesOrderLine.line_of link id; an order with more lines than one plx.around page is skipped and counted as orders_wide) and asks each order's lines through the served host (Host.served_tools) as its capture principal: plx.around from the order (reverse line_of at tier floor lead: each line's edge tier, and at the default floor which lines are counted), plx.aggregate over the order's lines (forward line_of grouped by order_number: counted, or under null with a below_tier_floor gap) and plx.process from the order's sales_order_lifecycle (names link_below_tier_floor for the line hop exactly when a line is a lead; never_authority_record is stricter about the record, never the link, and is only counted). Recorded: links asked, staging links asked, counted per tool (the process count is the around count of each order on which plx.process agrees), around tiers, disagreements (orders on which the tools differ) with their kinds, process record refusals and sources. Pass = no contract failure, no tool error, no disagreement, at least one link asked, and the counted totals of plx.aggregate and plx.process equal plx.around's. With no record source the probe names sources_blocked. Counts, booleans, tier names and source names only; never a value, key, identifier or citation. Live-unverified until the live check records a result.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check records a result. Module test: tests/test_link_tier_agree_probe.py (synthetic store with the real compiled schema and stage graphs: a same-source FK link between staging rows is counted at its tier by all three tools, a text-join link to a staging line is a lead in all three, and a tool that stops applying the shared rule, or a plx.process that names no lead link when a line is one, fails the probe); the tier rule itself is operating/tests/test_link_tier_rule.py. It builds cold in {tmp} and shares no session path, so it changes no session audience; it could instead require ontology.session_projection and read {session_state}/projection read-only. Timing (forecast, unmeasured): the build within 2,600 s, then at most 3 tool calls per order (60 calls).
